(task-criteria-4)=
# 4. Task facets and variants

A task record describes one **standard form** of the task, the one the
[inclusion test](03_the_task_inclusion_test.md) defines, and then lists its
**variants**: the other forms that whole studies run. A variant states only how it
differs from the standard form. Everything else about how studies vary a task goes
into the inclusion test as a manipulation or as an optional procedure step. This page
gives the rules for each, the rule for when a form becomes a task of its own, and the
policies for the borderline cases. The Catalog has {{ n_variants }} variants over
{{ n_tasks }} tasks. Every value named below is defined on the generated
[task vocabulary](../../tasks/vocabulary.md) page, and each task page shows its
standard form under "At a glance".

(task-criteria-4-1)=
## 4.1 What a task record says about how the task is run

Six things describe the standard form, besides the inclusion test.

- **Game type.** What the participant is doing, in one of ten kinds: respond under a
  rule, study then be tested, choose for a payoff, play against another player, solve
  a puzzle, make a movement, watch or listen, report on yourself, find the way, and
  hold a state.
- **Rules.** Each game type asks a few questions about how the game is played, such as
  "What competes with the correct response?" or "Who is the other player?". Each
  question has a default answer. A task states a rule only when its answer differs
  from the default, so a task that states no rules plays its game in the default way.
- **Motivation.** Why the participant tries. Every task answers "Why does the player
  try?"; where there is an outcome, the record also says whether the participant can
  gain, lose or both, what earns it, what it is, and whether it is real.
- **Facets.** What the participant sees, uses and is, in nine facets. Each facet lists
  the values that are present; a facet with nothing to say is left out.
  - Stimulus modality: which sense does the stimulus reach?
  - Stimulus type: what is the stimulus made of?
  - Emotional aspect: how is emotion built into the experiment?
  - Social aspect: how are other people built into the experiment?
  - Task I/O device: what equipment delivers the task and collects the response?
  - Trial structure: how is the run of trials delivered?
  - Feedback: does the participant learn how they did, and when?
  - Experimental environment: where is the participant while doing the task?
  - Population: who is there a version for?
- **Settings and material.** Settings name the quantities studies choose when they run
  the task (a retention interval, a set size, the proportion of congruent trials), with
  no numbers. Material is one sentence saying what the stimuli are.
- **Phases and combined games**, when the task has them. Phases name parts beyond the
  game's own structure (acquisition, extinction, transfer, devaluation, test). A
  combined game is a second game played with the first, and the record says how:
  in quick succession, throughout, interleaved, inserted, or chained.

The [Stroop Color-Word Task](../../tasks/hedtsk_stroop_color_word.md) is a game of
responding under a rule. It states one rule, that an irrelevant dimension competes with
the correct response; its motivation is instructions only; its facets are a visual
stimulus made of words, on a computer screen with a microphone, in fixed-time trials,
for young adults; its setting is the proportion congruent; and its material is "Color
words (RED, BLUE) printed in ink of a matching or a different color."

(task-criteria-4-2)=
## 4.2 What a variant is

A **variant** is an attested form of a task that a whole study uses, and that either
differs from the standard form in something the record can state or is a named
published instrument. The record can state a different facet value, a different rule
answer, a different motivation, a phase, a combined game, or a cognitive process the
form engages in addition to the standard form's.

A variant states only what differs and inherits the rest. A facet it names replaces the
standard form's values for that facet; an empty facet means the facet does not apply to
that form. A variant never restates the standard form: a value, a rule answer or a
motivation equal to the standard form's is left out. A variant may state a rule's
default to undo a rule the standard form states. Each variant has a name, a stored
identifier of the form `hedvar_<task>__<variant>`, and a one-paragraph note in plain
language.

Three variants of the Stroop task, as the record states them:

- **Manual (Button-Press) Stroop** changes the task I/O device to a computer screen and
  a keyboard: "The ink color is reported by key press, one key per color, instead of
  aloud."
- **Counting Stroop** changes one rule, so that the rule asks the participant to count:
  "A number word is printed one to four times and the participant reports how many
  words there are while ignoring the number named."
- **Face-Word Stroop** changes four facets and adds two processes, emotion recognition
  and face perception: "An emotion word is written across an expressive face and the
  participant names the expression while ignoring the word."

The [Anti-Saccade Task](../../tasks/hedtsk_anti_saccade.md) shows a variant undoing a
rule. Its standard form states that the participant responds away from the stimulus;
its variant Prosaccade (Control Condition) states the default answer, that the
participant responds on every trial in the ordinary way: "The same display but the
participant looks toward the cue, so the opposite-response demand is dropped."

A named instrument is a variant even when it changes nothing the record can state. Its
note says what it is, as for the Short Form WCST (64 Cards): "A named instrument using
only the first 64 cards with the same rules and scoring."

(task-criteria-4-3)=
## 4.3 What is not a variant

Three kinds of difference look like variants and are recorded elsewhere, or not at
all.

- **A factor varied within a study is a manipulation.** When one study compares levels
  of something (congruent and incongruent trials, short and long delays, load and no
  load), the factor goes into the task's inclusion test as one manipulation, one
  independent variable per item. Stroop's manipulations include "Congruency
  (congruent, incongruent, neutral)" and "Response modality (vocal, manual)". A form
  that some studies run throughout, such as the manual Stroop, can be a variant and
  also appear as one level of a manipulation.
- **A part that some studies add is an optional procedure step.** An extinction phase,
  a probe block or a transfer test that does not change the rest of the task goes into
  the inclusion test's procedure as a step that begins "Optional:".
- **A restatement of the standard form is nothing.** A "standard" or "classic" form, or
  a form that differs only in what the standard form already says, is not recorded.
  The vocal-response Stroop was removed for this reason: naming the ink color aloud is
  the standard form.

Things that never change the task are not recorded either: the recording equipment
(fMRI, EEG, eye tracking as a measure), the analysis or scoring method, a drug given
during the task, use of the task as a training intervention or an individual-differences
measure, and a stimulus set swapped for an equivalent one (IAPS for OASIS, a translated
word list). Testing a different population with an unchanged task is not a variant
either; see 4.5.3.

(task-criteria-4-4)=
## 4.4 When a form becomes a task of its own

A form is promoted to a task of its own when it has its own name in the literature, its
own procedure, and studies or mapping entries that cite it by that name rather than as
a version of the parent. A promoted task gets a full record, with its own inclusion
test, standard form and variants. Its parent no longer describes it, and its record
does not tell its history.

Four forms were promoted on 2026-11-17: the
[AX Continuous Performance Task](../../tasks/hedtsk_ax_continuous_performance.md) from
the Continuous Performance Task, the
[Dual N-Back Task](../../tasks/hedtsk_dual_n_back.md) from the N-Back Task, the
[Picture-Word Interference Task](../../tasks/hedtsk_picture_word_interference.md) from
the Picture Naming Task, and the [Tower of Hanoi Task](../../tasks/hedtsk_tower_of_hanoi.md)
from the Tower of London Task. Hybrid Search and the First-Person Shooter Task were
considered and stayed on their parents as variants.

(task-criteria-4-5)=
## 4.5 Borderline cases

Six kinds of form needed an explicit policy. Each is stated below in terms of the
record; the old open questions are answered where the record now answers them.

(task-criteria-4-5-1)=
### 4.5.1 Emotional versions

An emotional version of a task, in which the stimuli carry emotion or the participant
judges an emotion, is a variant when studies run it as a form of the task. It states
the emotional aspect facet, and usually a different stimulus type and the processes it
adds. Emotional Flanker is an example: "The central item and flankers are expressive
faces or pictures and the participant classifies the central emotion." Emotional
versions are not promoted to tasks of their own; this avoids a task for every pairing
of a paradigm with emotional stimuli. The Emotional Stroop Task, the Emotion
Regulation Task and the Facial Emotion Recognition Task are tasks because they were
always separate entries, not because they were promoted.

(task-criteria-4-5-2)=
### 4.5.2 Proportion congruent

The proportion of congruent trials is a setting, listed on six tasks (Attention
Network, Eriksen Flanker, Posner Spatial Cueing, Semantic Priming, Simon, and Stroop),
and a manipulation where studies compare levels of it. It is not a variant. The old
question, whether it is a design choice, is answered: it is a quantity a study
chooses, which is what a setting records.

(task-criteria-4-5-3)=
### 4.5.3 Child and developmental versions

A version for children is a variant when its procedure or its stimuli change, or when
it is a named published instrument. It states the population facet together with
whatever else changes. Child ANT is an example: "Cartoon fish replace the arrows,
trials are slower, feedback is given and the task is framed as feeding the fish." The
RMET Child Version is kept as a named instrument. Testing children with an unchanged
task is not a variant, and a stimulus set swapped only for age-appropriateness, with
the procedure unchanged, is not one either.

(task-criteria-4-5-4)=
### 4.5.4 Dual-task add-ons

A concurrent secondary task that studies add as a factor (load against no load,
articulatory suppression) is a manipulation of the main task, not a variant, however
common the pairing. The Serial Reaction Time Task's manipulation "Secondary task
(dual-task interference)" is an example. Where a second game is part of what defines a
form, the record states it as a combined game, on the standard form (the Psychological
Refractory Period Task) or on a variant (Subtest 2: Divided Attention of the Useful
Field of View Task).

(task-criteria-4-5-5)=
### 4.5.5 Confidence ratings and subjective reports

A confidence rating or subjective report added to an otherwise unchanged task is not a
variant and is not recorded. It adds a response, but by that logic any added scale
would make a new form. The exception is a named paradigm whose construct of interest
is the correspondence between confidence and accuracy itself. The one example is the Confidence-Accuracy Paradigm of the Heartbeat
Detection Task, where Garfinkel et al. (2015) made that correspondence one of the
measured dimensions of interoception: "After each trial the participant also rates
confidence in the answer."

(task-criteria-4-5-6)=
### 4.5.6 Computerized and manual versions

A computerized version is a variant only when it changes the equipment the participant
uses or the movement they make, which the task I/O device facet states: physical blocks
replaced by squares touched on a screen (Computerized (eCorsi)), handwriting replaced by
key presses (Computerized DSST/SDMT). A stylus on a tablet in place of a pencil on paper
is the same movement and not a variant. Software that only administers or scores the
task is never a variant. A computerized form can be a variant for another reason: the
Computerized Adaptive Version of Raven's Progressive Matrices chooses each item from
the answers so far, and the Prisoner's Dilemma played against a computer program
changes who the other player is.
